name: [BUAMS] KUL 2 ADULT LEARNING (YOS)
text:
ADULT LEARNING
Oleh:
Yossi Indra Kusuma, S.Ked., M.Med.Ed.
Tujuan Pembelajaran
• Menjelaskan definisi Pembelajaran
• Mengetahui Teori-teori Pembelajaran
• Memahami tentang Self Directed Learning
• Menjelaskan prinsip, konsep dan karakteristik 
pembelajaran orang dewasa
• Menjelaskan perbedaan antara pedagogy dan 
andragogy
• Menjelaskan empat elemen penting dalam pembelajaran 
orang dewasa
• Memahami proses belajar orang dewasa
MENGAPA 
HARUS 
BELAJAR?
Definisi
Apa itu belajar???
Perubahan yang menetap dalam hal perilaku atau dalam kapasitas kemampuan 
untuk berperilaku dengan cara tertentu yang dihasilkan dari pengalaman (Shuell, 
1986) 
Perubahan yang menetap dalam performa manusia atau performa potensial 
sebagai hasil dari interaksi pembelajar dengan lingkungannya (Driscoll, 1993) 
Proses yang menghasilkan perubahan periaku yang relatif menetap tentang 
cara berpikir, berperasaan dan bertingkah laku dari pembelajar ( Coates, 2006)
Pembelajaran merupakan perubahan yang bertahan lama dalam perilaku, atau 
dalam kapasitas berperilaku dengan cara tertentu, yang dihasilkan dari praktik atau 
bentuk-bentuk pengalaman lainnya (Schunk, 2012)
Learning Theory
Paradigms in Learning
(Penchion D. 1999.  Editorial BMJ.  May 8)
OLD Paradigm
•
Finite amount of knowledge to be 
absorbed
•
Experts are recognized by knowing 
what they should know
•
Learning starts by contacting an 
authority
•
Uncertainty is discouraged and 
ignorance avoided
•
Experts have knowledge
NEW Paradigm
•
It is not possible to absorb all 
knowledge on a subject
•
Experts are recognized by knowing 
what they don’t know and knowing 
how to manage it
•
Learning starts in practice
•
Legitimizing uncertainty and learning 
by questioning
•
Experts find solutions
SELF DIRECTED LEARNING
Suatu proses dimana seseorang memiliki inisiatif, dengan atau tanpa bantuan 
orang lain untuk menganalisis kebutuhan belajarnya sendiri, merumuskan tujuan 
belajarnya sendiri, mengidentifikasi sumber-sumber belajar, memilih dan 
melaksanakan strategi belajar yang sesuai serta mengevaluasi hasil belajarnya 
sendiri 
   
       (Knowles, 1975 cited in Mulube, 2014)
Meliputi bagaimana mahasiswa belajar setiap harinya, bagaimana 
mahasiswa dapat menyesuaikan diri dengan keadaan yang cepat berubah, 
dan bagaimana mahasiswa dapat mengambil inisiatifnya sendiri
   
 
               (Gibbons, 2003)
Memberi kesempatan kepada Mahasiswa untuk menetukan desain 
pembelajaran mereka sendiri, dari tujuan belajar, rencana proses belajar, 
sumber-sumber belajar yang dipilih, pembuatan keputusan-keputusan 
akademik, dan sampai kegiatan-kegiatan untuk mencapai tujuan belajar tsb
   
 
       (Nyambe, 2015)

ADULT LEARNING
Definisi
• Merupakan pengalaman belajar 
berdasarkan kebutuhan dan minat orang 
dewasa pada tingkatan kemampuan dan 
pengetahuan yang berbeda untuk 
mendukung perubahan peranan serta 
tanggung jawab dalam kehidupannya
Andragogy vs Pedagogy
• Andragogy
– Andr
= Adult  orang dewasa
– Agogos
= Leading  membimbing
– Ilmu dan kiat membimbing orang dewasa
• Pedagogy :
– Paid
= Child  anak
– Agogos
= Leading  membimbing
– Ilmu dan kiat membimbing / mengajar anak
Pengertian
• Andragogy / Adult Learning
– Kiat dan Ilmu tentang membantu orang dewasa 
belajar (the art and science of helping adults 
learn)
• Pedagogy
– Kiat dan Ilmu tentang mendidik atau mengajar 
anak-anak (the art and science of educating and 
often is used as synonym for teaching)

Characteristics of Learners
ADULT LEARNERS
• Problem-centered
• Results-oriented
• Self-directed
• Often skeptical about 
new information
• Seek relevancy
• Accepts responsibility for 
own learning
YOUTH LEARNERS
• Subject-oriented
• Future-oriented
• Often depend on adults 
for direction
• More accepting
• Often train for unclear 
future
• Often dependent on 
others

The 4 Elements
Self directed learning
• Organizing teaching and 
learning so that learning is 
within the learners’ control
• A goal towards which 
learners strive so that they 
become able to accept 
responsibility for their own 
learning
SELF EFFICAFY
• Bandura posits that people’s 
judgments of their own ability 
to deal with different 
situations is central to their 
actions
• 4 sources: performance 
attainments, observations of 
others, verbal persuasion, and 
physiological state
Constructivism
• The primary idea of 
constructivism is that learners 
“construct” their own knowledge 
on the basis of what they already 
know
• This theory posits that learning is 
active, rather than passive, with 
learners making judgments about 
when and how to modify their 
knowledge.
Teacher’s role
is a
FACILITATOR
Learning 
based
on prior
knowledge
Active
learning
Is key
Reflective practice
• Ability to reflect on one’s 
actions so as to engage in a 
process of continous learning
• Formal theory often not useful 
to solve real life problems
• Reflection in action
• Reflection on action
How Adult Learns
(Taylor & Hamdy, 2013)
Dissonance Phase
•
existing knowledge is 
challenged and found to be 
incomplete 
•
Internal or external
•
Nature of the task, available 
resources, motivation, stage of 
development and preferred 
learning style influence the 
engagement
•
It ends with the learner 
reflecting and determining their 
personal learning outcomes 
Dissonance Phase
Learner’s Role :
•
Identify prior (baseline) 
knowledge, skills and 
attitudes 
•
Recognise what is unknown 
•
Recognise personal 
development and learning 
needs 
•
Participate in planning 
personal learning objectives 
and relevant experiences 
Refinement Phase
•
the learner seeks out a 
number of possible 
explanations or solutions to a 
problem (elaboration)
•
through completing tasks, 
research, reflection and 
discussion refines the new 
information into a series of 
concepts which are, for the 
learner, NEW !
Refinement Phase
Learner’s Role :
•
Think of many possible 
explanations or solutions to 
the case or problem. 
•
Work out which are the most 
likely resources to refine the 
possibilities 
•
Actively participate in the 
activity and experiences 
•
Refine the information into a 
hypothesis 
Organization Phase
•
the learner develops or 
restructures their ideas to 
account for the increased 
information they have acquired
•
There are at least two elements 
to this:
– reflection in action : where 
the learner tests and re-
tests hypotheses to makes 
sense of the information
– organisation of the 
information into schemata 
which (for the learner, at 
least) make sense. 
Organization Phase
Learner’s Role :
• Test and re-test the 
hypothesis 
• Organise the information 
into a ‘‘story’’ that makes 
sense to the learner 
Feedback Phase
•
the most crucial
•
the learner articulates their 
newly acquired knowledge 
and tests it against what 
their peers and teachers 
believe
•
the feedback will either 
reinforce their schema, or 
oblige the learner to 
reconsider it in the light of 
new information
Feedback Phase
Learner’s Role :
•
Articulate the knowledge, 
skills or attitudes 
developed 
•
Provide feedback to peers 
and staff 
•
Accept, and if appropriate 
act upon feedback received 
from others 
Consolidation Phase
The learner reflects upon 
the process they have 
undergone, looking back 
over the learning cycle and 
identifying what they have 
learned from it, both in 
terms of increasing their 
knowledge base, but also in 
terms of the learning 
process itself (reflection on 
action) 
Consolidation Phase
Learner’s Role :
•
Reflection in the light of prior 
knowledge 
•
Reflection on the learning 
process 
•
Evaluate personal 
responsibility for the learning
•
Development of knowledge, 
skills and attitudes
